data.title: Rubico Announces $8.5 Million Registered Direct Offering of Senior Convertible Notes and Warrants
data.description:
ATHENS, Greece, Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Rubico Inc. (the "Company," "Rubico," “we” or “us”), a global provider of shipping transportation services specializing in the ownership of vessels, today announced it has entered into a securities purchase agreement (the “Purchase Agreement”) with a single institutional investor (the “Holder”) to issue senior convertible notes (the “Notes”) in the aggregate principal amount of $9,444,444, bearing an original issue discount of 10% and warrants (the “Warrants”) to purchase common shares with an aggregate initial cash exercise price of $9,444,444. The Company expects to issue such Notes and Warrants on or about October 19, 2026 (the “First Tranche Closing”), subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions. The Company will receive gross proceeds of $8,500,000 at the First Tranche Closing.

The Notes are unsecured and will bear an interest rate of 8.00% per annum if paid in cash and 10.00% per annum if paid in Common Shares. The Notes will mature 12 months after issuance, subject to extension at the Company’s option to 18 months, provided that upon such extension the principal amount of the applicable Note will be increased by 5%. The Notes will be convertible at a conversion price equal to the lower of the closing price of the Company’s common shares immediately prior to issuance or the average closing price over the five days prior to issuance (the “Fixed Conversion Price”). The Fixed Conversion Price with respect to the First Tranche Closing will be $0.3646. The Notes are also convertible at the Holder’s option at an alternate conversion price equal to the greater of 85% of the lowest daily volume-weighted average price of the Company’s common shares during the 10 trading days preceding the conversion date and a floor price of $0.10.

The warrants will be immediately exercisable, will expire on the five-year anniversary of the issuance date and will have an initial exercise price equal to the Fixed Conversion Price. At the First Tranche Closing the Company expects to issue Warrants exercisable to purchase 25,903,577 common shares at an exercise price of $0.3646 per share.

In addition, subject to certain conditions set forth in the Purchase Agreement, the Company may issue and sell to the Holder in a second closing (the “Second Tranche Closing”) an additional $5,555,556 in aggregate principal amount of the Notes and Warrants to purchase common shares with an aggregate initial cash exercise price of $5,555,556. The Company would receive gross proceeds of $5,000,000 at the Second Tranche Closing.

In addition, at each of the First Tranche Closing and the Second Tranche Closing, the Company has agreed pursuant to the Purchase Agreement to issue a number of common shares (and/or pre-funded warrants in lieu thereof) (“Commitment Shares”) to the Holder equal to 5% of the face value of the principal amount of the Notes issued at each closing divided by the Fixed Conversion Price with respect to the relevant tranche. At the First Tranche Closing the Company expects to issue 1,295,179 Commitment Shares (and/or pre-funded warrants in lieu thereof).

Maxim Group LLC is acting as the sole placement agent in connection with the offering.

The securities described above are being offered pursuant to a shelf registration statement on Form F-3 (File No. 333-297207), which was declared effective by the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”) on July 14, 2026. A prospectus supplement relating to the securities to be issued in the Offering will be filed by the Company with the SEC. When available, copies of the prospectus supplement relating to the Offering, together with the accompanying prospectus, can be obtained at the SEC's website at www.sec.gov or by contacting Maxim Group LLC, at 300 Park Avenue, 16th Floor, New York, NY 10022, Attention: Syndicate Department, or via email at syndicate@maximgrp.com or by telephone at (212) 895-3745.

This press release does not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy, nor will there be any sales of these securities in any jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful prior to registration or qualification under the securities laws of such jurisdiction.

About the Company

Rubico Inc. is a global provider of shipping transportation services specializing in the ownership of vessels. The Company is an international owner and operator of two modern, fuel efficient, eco 157,000 dwt Suezmax tankers. Furthermore, the Company owns three 47,499 dwt MR tanker newbuildings scheduled for delivery in the second, third and fourth quarters of 2029 and a 60-meter newbuilding megayacht scheduled for delivery in the second quarter of 2027, which the Company intends to divest.

The Company is incorporated under the laws of the Republic of the Marshall Islands and has executive offices in Athens, Greece. The Company's common shares trade on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol "RUBI".

data.title: VCI Global Advances AI Infrastructure and Token Services Strategy; Strengthens Balance Sheet in 1H2026
data.description:
Total Equity Increases 19.2% to US$114.70 Million as Company Prioritizes Expansion Across GPU Computing and AI Model Service

KUALA LUMPUR, Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- VCI Global Limited (“VCI Global” or the “Company”), today announced its unaudited financial results for the six months ended June 30, 2026 (“1H2026”), as it advances its strategic transition toward AI computing, AI token services and infrastructure-related opportunities.

The first half of 2026 marked a significant transition for VCI Global following the separation and divestment of its capital markets consultancy, fintech and other non-core businesses. The Company is now concentrating its resources and capital allocation on building AI computing capabilities, commercializing AI services and developing infrastructure opportunities across the AI value chain.

At the same time, VCI Global is pursuing complementary opportunities in renewable energy, energy storage and carbon assets as it works toward a broader infrastructure model connecting AI, computing, energy and sustainability.

  • Total equity increased 19.2% to US$114.70 million as of June 30, 2026, compared with US$96.21 million as compared to December 31, 2025.
  • Total liabilities declined 17.7% to US$17.03 million from US$20.69 million over the same period.
  • Cash and bank balances rose more than fivefold to US$5.19 million from US$0.94 million, supported by financing activities and the disposal of an investment.
  • Revenue was US$2.56 million, compared with US$18.74 million in 1H2025, reflecting the Group’s portfolio restructuring and changes in its operating profile.
  • VGAIN Compute was launched, providing customers with a platform to purchase AI tokens and access multiple supported large language models, including OpenAI GPT, Kimi, Meta Llama and Qwen.
  • Acquisition of the controlling stake in PT Fine Carbon Credit Indonesia (FCCI), an Indonesian carbon asset platform associated with approximately 241,000 hectares of forestry areas across four project sites.

“The first half of 2026 represents an important inflection point for VCI Global as we reposition the Company around AI infrastructure and scalable technology services,” said Ang Zhi Feng, Chief Financial Officer of VCI Global. “While revenue declined as a result of the transition, we ended the period with higher total equity, lower liabilities and an increased cash balance. Our priority is to manage liquidity carefully and allocate capital to initiatives with clear commercial potential as we advance our AI services and infrastructure strategy.”

REVENUE REFLECTS PORTFOLIO RESTRUCTURING

The first half of 2026 represents a fundamental change in VCI Global’s operating profile.

The Company has completed the separation and divestment of its capital markets consultancy, fintech, and other non-core businesses, reducing exposure to businesses that were not aligned with its longer-term technology and infrastructure strategy.

Revenue for 1H2026 was US$2.56 million, compared with US$18.74 million in 1H2025. The decrease primarily reflects businesses that have since been separated or divested, along with the transition to a more focused AI infrastructure and technology operating model.

CASH POSITION AND CAPITAL ALLOCATION

As of June 30, 2026, total equity increased 19.2% to US$114.70 million from US$96.21 million at December 31, 2025, while total liabilities declined 17.7% to US$17.03 million from US$20.69 million.

Cash and bank balances increased to US$5.19 million from US$0.94 million at year-end 2025. The increase was supported by financing activities and the disposal of an investment.

The Company intends to prioritize capital deployment based on commercial demand, financing availability and project readiness, with investment priorities spanning AI Infrastructure, GPU computing and related infrastructure.

VGAIN COMPUTE: FROM AI ACCESS TO AI CONSUMPTION

VCI Global announced the launch of VGAIN Compute on October 6, 2026, through its subsidiary V Gallant Limited.

The platform enables users to purchase AI tokens to access supported large language models, including OpenAI GPT, Kimi, Meta Llama and Qwen. Announced applications include content generation, coding, research, business applications and workflow automation.

The platform introduces a customer-facing offering through which VCI Global can pursue revenue from AI services. Its token-based model provides a mechanism for charging users for access to supported AI capabilities.

The broader market opportunity is expanding as businesses move AI from experimentation into production. Gartner forecasts worldwide AI-optimised IaaS spending of US$42.3 billion in 2026, rising to US$66.1 billion in 2027. Gartner also estimates that global spending on AI inference infrastructure will reach US$23.3 billion in 2026, exceeding the US$19 billion forecast for AI model training infrastructure.

The Company’s next priorities include expanding platform usage, evaluating additional models and developing enterprise and developer applications.

DEVELOPING AN INTEGRATED POWER–AI–CARBON ECOSYSTEM

VCI Global’s longer-term infrastructure strategy extends beyond computing capacity to the resources required to support the expansion of AI infrastructure, including electricity generation, solar power, energy storage and data center operations.

The Company intends to develop an integrated infrastructure model designed to connect energy supply with computing demand, with the objective of improving power availability, supporting scalable AI computing and enhancing long-term operating efficiency.

As AI workloads become increasingly compute-intensive, access to reliable and scalable power is becoming an increasingly important consideration in the development of data center and GPU infrastructure. VCI Global believes that combining computing infrastructure with energy development can provide greater control over critical infrastructure requirements as its AI businesses expand.

LONGER-TERM OPPORTUNITIES IN ENERGY AND FOREST CONSERVATION

VCI Global announced that V Gallant had entered into a definitive agreement to acquire a 70% stake in PT Fine Carbon Credit Indonesia (FCCI), a platform associated with approximately 241,000 hectares of forestry areas across four project sites in Indonesia.

The proposed acquisition provides a potential basis for developing forestry-linked carbon credit projects, subject to transaction completion and applicable technical, legal and regulatory requirements.

The voluntary carbon market offers a potential monetization route for eligible forestry projects, but credit prices vary significantly according to project type, certification standard, carbon integrity, vintage, and buyer demand.

According to Ecosystem Marketplace’s 2025 State of the Voluntary Carbon Market report, based on 2024 transactions, the average price was approximately US$14.97 per tonne of CO₂ equivalent for improved forest management credits and US$20.44 for tree-planting and restoration credits. Some premium credits may command prices above US$50, depending on their characteristics and market conditions.

COMMERCIAL PRIORITIES AND INVESTOR MILESTONES

VCI Global’s initiatives cover several potential sources of revenue, each with different development requirements.

  • AI services: VGAIN Compute provides a live platform through which the Company can pursue paid AI model access. Commercial performance can be assessed through active paying users, token consumption, revenue and service delivery costs.
  • GPU cloud services: VGAIN Cloud is intended to support demand for AI computing. Relevant milestones include infrastructure deployment, available GPU capacity, customer contracts, utilisation and revenue generated from computing services.
  • AI data center infrastructure: Galatron AI Factory’s initial planned 5MW deployment provides a defined development milestone within the broader 500MW roadmap. Progress will depend on site readiness, power availability, funding and customer demand.
  • Energy infrastructure: Potential revenue opportunities depend on the development and ownership of specific projects, available generation or storage capacity, and contracted demand.
  • Carbon assets: FCCI represents a potential forestry-linked carbon credit opportunity. Key milestones include transaction completion, project qualification, credit issuance and actual sales.

These indicators provide a clearer basis for evaluating the Company’s progress than global market growth alone.

OUTLOOK

The global expansion of AI infrastructure presents opportunities across model access, cloud computing, data center development and supporting energy infrastructure. VCI Global has announced initiatives across these areas, beginning with the launch of VGAIN Compute and extending to planned computing infrastructure and complementary asset opportunities.

The Company’s ability to benefit from these markets will depend on execution and commercial validation. Market forecasts indicate the scale of industry investment, but they do not establish VCI Global’s future revenue, market share or profitability.

VCI Global intends to progress its initiatives in phases, with the commercial outcomes of each business dependent on customer demand, operating performance, capital availability, project milestones and applicable regulatory requirements.

“Our ambition is to build an AI infrastructure business that connects customer demand, computing capacity and the energy required to support it,” said Victor Hoo, Group Chief Executive Officer and Executive Chairman of VCI Global. “VGAIN Compute provides a commercial entry point for building customer relationships and recurring usage, while our infrastructure strategy creates opportunities to participate more deeply in the AI value chain. Over the longer term, we see the potential to develop an integrated model in Asia that brings together AI computing, energy and forest conservation.”

“We intend to demonstrate the value of this transition through execution. That means growing customer usage, bringing productive computing capacity into service and converting commercial opportunities into revenue. Those are the milestones that will define the next phase of VCI Global.” He added.

Management will continue to emphasize commercial validation, disciplined capital allocation and phased execution. The pace of development and contribution from individual initiatives will depend on customer demand, funding, regulatory considerations and project milestones.

About VCI Global Limited

VCI Global Limited is transforming into an AI infrastructure and technology group focused on AI computing, GPU infrastructure and AI token services through its businesses, including V Gallant and VGAIN Compute. Following the spin-off and divestment of its capital markets consultancy, fintech and other non-core businesses, the Company is sharpening its focus on AI-driven growth while exploring complementary opportunities in renewable energy, power generation, energy storage and forest conservation, including potential carbon credit initiatives. Through these interconnected areas, VCI Global aims to build a scalable and sustainable infrastructure platform supported by disciplined capital allocation and long-term value creation.

data.title: Anthropic signs lease for first Canadian data center
data.description:
Anthropic has signed a lease with EverWind for data center capacity at Point Tupper, Nova Scotia, marking the Claude maker’s first data center agreement in Canada, a company executive said on Friday.

Here are some more details:

  • Separately, EverWind unveiled plans to invest more than C$10 billion in the data center campus and wind power projects in Nova Scotia, calling it the largest privately funded investment in the province’s history.

  • Data centers have faced criticism over their heavy power and water use and the strain they place on local infrastructure.

  • Jacob Glick, Anthropic’s head of public policy for Canada, said the company would protect ratepayers and water resources while ensuring local communities benefit.

  • Anthropic spent $7.33 billion on computing and infrastructure last year, a threefold surge from 2024.

  • The company is preparing for a US IPO that could value it at more than $2 trillion, although New York City Comptroller Mark Levine has urged it to delay the offering over safety and governance concerns.

data.title: XCF Global CEO Updates Shareholders Following Recent Market Volatility
data.description:
HOUSTON, TX / ACCESS Newswire / October 16, 2026 / XCF Global, Inc. today shared the following update with shareholders:

"We understand that the recent volatility and decline in our share price have been concerning and frustrating for our shareholders, and we take those concerns seriously. We value the confidence our shareholders have placed in XCF and believe it is important to communicate openly about the progress we are making and the priorities that continue to guide us.

Although short-term market movements are outside our control, we remain firmly focused on what we can control: executing our strategy, managing our resources responsibly, strengthening our business, and creating sustainable long-term value for our shareholders.

Over the past several months, we believe XCF has made meaningful progress in transitioning our Reno facility from development and commissioning to commercial operations. We reported more than $10 million in revenue for August and over $12 million in gross product sales (a non-GAAP financial measure) for September, with daily production reaching approximately 85,000 gallons by the end of September. These milestones reflect tangible progress in building our business and the dedication of our team. We believe this progress positions XCF to respond to continued growth in demand for renewable fuels, supported by the expansion of low-carbon fuel programs across a growing number of states.

Today, we also announced the closing of our business combination with Southern Energy Renewables and DevvStream, as we work toward advancing our broader strategy to build a diversified energy platform.

We recognize that operational progress must ultimately translate into sustainable profitability, greater financial strength, and long-term shareholder value. Our management team and Board remain focused on these priorities, including disciplined capital allocation, responsible management of our capital structure, and protection of our shareholders' long-term interests.

We know that shareholder confidence is earned through execution, transparency, and results. We are holding ourselves to that standard and intend to demonstrate our progress through measurable operating performance and clear, consistent communication.

On behalf of our management team and Board of Directors, I thank our shareholders for their continued engagement and support. We remain focused on building a stronger XCF and creating long-term value for those who have invested in our future. Our responsibility is not simply to grow the business, but to ensure that the value created by that growth benefits our shareholders over the long term."

Chris Cooper

Chief Executive Officer

XCF Global, Inc.

About XCF Global, Inc.

XCF Global, Inc. is a U.S.-based producer of renewable diesel and SAF focused on decarbonizing transportation while supporting domestic fuel supply, energy security and alternative uses for agricultural waste products. Its New Rise Renewables Reno facility has permitted nameplate capacity of 38 - 40 million gallons per year. XCF trades on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol SAFX. To learn more, visit xcf.global.

data.title: New Cracks in AI Trade Push Wall Street to Worst Week Since June — WSJ
data.description:
By Sam Goldfarb, Gunjan Banerji and Jack Pitcher

It was the week Wall Street wavered on America's Teflon economy.

A top chipmaker's chief executive likened some AI investors' behavior to gambling. Reports of Chinese advances in semiconductors added fuel to a rout in chip stocks. A hot inflation report sent the bond market on a roller coaster and, along the way, one of the most prominent AI cloud companies had a meltdown in both the equity and debt markets.

A broad tech selloff Friday punctuated the market's worst week since June as the Nasdaq composite tumbled 4.5%.

Hovering over all of it were fears among investors that the higher borrowing costs in the U.S. might slow the historic investments in artificial-intelligence infrastructure that have become an all-important driver of economic growth. That, in turn, led to a flight back to government bonds, ending a bruising selloff that had driven Treasury yields to their highest levels in more than two decades.

As bonds rallied, the yield on the 10-year Treasury note fell 0.146 percentage point to 5.097%, according to Tradeweb — its biggest weekly decline since mid-February, before the start of the Iran war.

The week's events bolstered the arguments of investors like Ben Inker, co-head of asset allocation at Boston-based money manager GMO, who has been a vocal bear of the AI trade.

He points to prior periods of heavy investment such as the railroad boom and mania around dot-com stocks, which led to market busts. To him, AI is no different from those frenzies.

"If AI spending does not continue to grow, that gets tough for aggregate demand," Inker said. "It's likely that if AI really slows down, it will be really bad on the economy."

One recent warning sign? Rising borrowing costs for AI companies, along with a looming deluge in share issuance from companies including Anthropic and OpenAI. "You've got to bribe the lenders that much more to take more data center risk," Inker said.

The fears this week trickled through far-reaching corners of the market.

Riskier and more heavily indebted companies such as the cloud computing upstart CoreWeave took the brunt of the blow, with CoreWeave shares sliding 12% on Friday and 25% for the week. But the selloff swept through the wider tech sector, bringing down everyone from giant hyperscalers Amazon.com and Alphabet to highflying chip stocks Micron and Advanced Micro Devices.

The PHLX semiconductor index, packed with AI heavyweights like Nvidia and Broadcom, slid 3.8% on Friday to mark its longest losing streak since 2008. Dell Technologies plunged 22% this week, its worst weekly performance on record.

The swoon in stocks highlighted the close linkages between the economy, markets and a relatively small group of technology highfliers. There are roughly 45 S&P 500 companies deemed as having material exposure to artificial intelligence. Together, those companies have made up around 39% of the index's 14.1% return through Oct. 11, according to S&P Dow Jones Indices.

"AI is not only the economy, but it has become the equity market and a dominant force in the bond market too," Barclays strategists wrote in a recent note to clients.

The S&P 500 fell 1.1% on Friday, bringing its weekly loss to 1.9%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average, which carries relatively little exposure to tech, edged lower by 0.3%, or 175 points. The blue-chip index eked out a gain of 0.7% for the week.

Many see the AI trade, once a monolithic bet on chip stocks and hyperscalers, splintering. "Picks-and-shovels" companies making AI hardware are better-positioned than those relying on "cheap borrowed money to expand," said Michael Landsberg, chief investment officer at Landsberg Bennett Private Wealth Management.

"This is not a riskless trade. There's definitely going to be winners and losers," said Landsberg.

Warning signs started to flash in the trading of bonds tied to data-center companies this week, many of which fell sharply. The losses started with the riskiest and most indebted companies, like CoreWeave, but by Friday were showing up in data-center bonds with investment-grade ratings. Analysts said a Thursday announcement that Apple and Meta would team up on new AI models that run locally on a laptop, rather than at data centers, added to concerns.

For months, U.S. Treasury yields had been propelled higher by a mixture of pessimism about inflation and optimism about economic growth. Investors have thought that the Federal Reserve would raise rates further to fight inflation but that it would take much higher rates to seriously curb economic growth powered by an AI build-out seemingly unaffected by changes in borrowing costs.

Investors still expect the Fed to raise rates again — if not this month, then soon thereafter.

Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh said little about his thinking on rates in a public appearance Friday morning local time in Bangkok. Investors took that to mean that the central bank likely won't raise rates at its Oct. 27-28 meeting given that other officials have previously signaled that a pause was likely. But interest-rate futures indicate that traders still see a roughly 85% chance that the Fed will raise rates by the end of the year, with this week's hot inflation data only cementing those bets.

Some debt analysts focused on the tech sector remain skeptical that companies will slow their investments in AI infrastructure just because they are facing higher borrowing costs.

For one thing, they say, companies have already funded much of the spending that they plan to do over the next year or so. Demand for AI computing power also remains so high that even riskier companies have huge incentives to keep investing and finance their expenditures through whatever means possible.

"In order to really create a slowdown, you need to have the demand slow down," said Rich Gross, a senior fixed-income analyst at Columbia Threadneedle Investments. He added, though, that rising rates could curb AI investment in other ways, such as by hurting consumers and generally slowing the economy.

data.title: LQR House Inc. Announces CEO Transition
data.description:
Sean Dollinger Steps Down as Chief Executive Officer

Leo Chen Named CEO

MIAMI BEACH, FL / ACCESS Newswire / October 16, 2026 / LQR House Inc. (the "Company", "LQR House" or "LQR") today announced that Sean Dollinger has stepped down as Chief Executive Officer, effective October 16, 2026. Leo Chen will become Chief Executive Officer, effective immediately.

This change follows LQR's strategic pivot toward its New Zealand-based acquisition, Fusion Five Continents Securities, alongside several other initiatives, including a technology agreement with ByteDance. Mr. Dollinger believes the Company will be better served by a Chief Executive Officer with the operational background for this new direction. In connection with Mr. Dollinger's departure from LQR House, the online spirits business will be transferred to a company owned by Kumar Abhishek, the outgoing CFO of LQR House.

Mr. Chen has over 10 years of executive management experience in large enterprises and diversified conglomerates. He is the former Chairman of Shenzhen Jincheng Confidentiality Technology Co., Ltd., and served as the General Manager of the Finance Department of Beijing Energy International Holdings Co., Ltd. He has a master's degree in Economics from the University of Sydney, as well as a bachelor's in Business Management, with a concentration in Financial Management. As CEO, Mr. Chen will oversee day-to-day operations and the continued execution of LQR's strategy.

As founder and Chief Executive Officer, Mr. Dollinger led LQR House from inception through its August 2023 initial public offering on NASDAQ and into a period of sustained capital formation and strategic expansion.

"I founded LQR House to build a spirits e-commerce and marketing company, and taking it to NASDAQ with the LQR team is something I will always be proud of," said Mr. Dollinger. "Together with the Board, we have charted a new direction for the company, centered on Fusion Five Continents Securities in New Zealand and AI compute for quantitative research under an agreement with ByteDance. That direction calls for a CEO whose experience is closely aligned with those areas. Stepping aside now is the right decision for me and for the company. I will continue to work on the spirits e-commerce and marketing company outside the public capital markets, while also turning my attention to new projects in Artificial Intelligence, and I will support Leo and the Board through the transition."

"On behalf of the Board, I want to thank Sean for founding LQR House and taking it public," said Mr. Lijun Chen (no relation to Leo Chen), Non Executive Chairman and Director of LQR House. "During his tenure, Sean led the company through significant capital raises and strategic transactions, and he made this current decision with LQR's next phase in mind. We look forward to his continued support during the transition."

Mr. Chen added, "Leo's strong finance background and years of executive experience will serve the company well as we develop Fusion Five Continents Securities into a truly AI-enabled brokerage platform, integrating financial research, portfolio analytics, and investment execution. The Board is confident in Leo's ability as CEO to drive LQR's next phase. I look forward to working closely with him and the senior leadership team to execute on our strategy."

About LQR House Inc.

LQR House has transitioned from the wine and spirits e-commerce sector to operating as a cross-border securities trading intermediary. Through its subsidiary Fusion Five Continents Securities, LQR House provides clients with access to U.S. and Hong Kong equity markets through an integrated operational framework that offers AI-driven research, quantitative analytics, and automated portfolio optimization. Distinguishing it from most financial intermediaries targeting Asian investors, Fusion Five is able to accept USDT deposits as a funding mechanism for securities trading, with settlement facilitated by a licensed trust company, subject to applicable regulatory requirements. Fusion Five has assembled an experienced technology team with credentials from Oxford, Stockholm University, and Tsinghua University, combining expertise in quantitative finance, AI, and behavioral data science. Fusion Five is deploying AI-driven capabilities across its operations to drive efficiency and enhance the client experience, while advancing its vision of an AI-enabled brokerage platform integrating financial research, portfolio analytics, and investment execution.

data.title: Global hedge funds hammered by AI selloff this week, Asia managers lead losses
data.description:
Key points:
  • Global fundamental long-short funds lost 2.9% in week to October 15
  • Asia-focused stock pickers lost 6.8% in first half of October

By Summer Zhen and Anirban Sen

Global hedge funds suffered steep losses this week after being battered by the sharp unwind of a swathe of AI bets, with Asia-focused funds hit the hardest.

Investors are increasingly questioning whether massive AI spending can pay off anytime soon as elevated inflation keeps borrowing costs high. Wall Street ended the week sharply lower on Friday, with AI-related technology stocks including CoreWeave and Broadcom under renewed pressure, while a jump in oil prices spooked traders heading into the weekend.

CoreWeave has been one of the biggest casualties of the latest selloff, with the data center operator's bonds selling off sharply this week, pushing yields above 15%.

Global fundamental long-short funds, or stock pickers, lost money every single day this week, the Goldman Sachs prime brokerage unit said in a note to clients, with losses for the week to October 15 coming to 2.9%. For the year to date, they have gains of 14.3%.

"Following a sharp AI unwind on Wednesday and week-over-week, global equities were net sold again yesterday (Thursday) though at a much slower pace, driven by continued risk unwinds with long sales outpacing short covers. In dollar terms, yesterday's global de-grossing activity — long selling and short covering combined — was roughly half of what we saw on Wednesday," Goldman said in the note on Friday.

Goldman added that global AI stocks collectively have been sold by long-short fund managers for six straight sessions.

On Thursday, hedge funds across strategies retreated sharply, with stock pickers globally losing 0.9%. Among them, Asia-focused managers were down 2.6%, while tech-focused funds were off 2.0%.

Global systematic long-short managers and multi-strategy funds also declined roughly 1%.

Hotter-than-expected US inflation data this week that increased expectations of further rate ⁠hikes also fueled the selloff in semiconductor and AI supply chain stocks.

"From COVID through end-2025, all three broad strategies never fell more than 80 bps on the same day," Goldman Sachs said in an earlier note from Thursday, adding that this has now occurred three times this year, on February 4, July 28 and October 15.

Semiconductor-heavy markets bore the brunt of the selloff. South Korea's benchmark KOSPI tumbled 8% to close at a ‌six-month low on Thursday, while Taiwan stocks also lost more than 3%.

Asia-focused stock pickers have lost 6.8% for the first half of this month and have erased more than half of the gains from their late-June peak, when they were up more than 40% for the year, according to Goldman Sachs.

data.title: US air traffic controllers to get 2.8% pay raise under FAA deal
data.description:
By David Shepardson and Doyinsola Oladipo

Thousands of US air traffic controllers will get a 2.8% pay raise retroactive to January 1 under a deal announced by the Federal Aviation Administration and a union.

  • The pay raise, which was authorized by Congress, will be effective October 18

  • Controllers previously received a 1% raise but the remainder of the $140 million raise was contingent on workforce reforms

  • The agreed changes include tracking of controllers' time, aligning staffing with demand, and improving controller reassignments

  • The FAA has been working to address a persistent shortage of air traffic controllers

  • Many are working mandatory overtime and six-day weeks

  • Local managers and union representatives will now develop shift guidelines based on anticipated workload and operational requirements to ensure more productive controller schedules that maximize coverage during peak traffic hours

data.title: Anthropic quietly pitches its own AI safety bill to lawmakers, Politico reports
data.description:
Anthropic representatives have quietly pitched Capitol Hill lawmakers on a draft bill to regulate frontier AI safety and security, Politico reported on Friday, citing three people with knowledge of the efforts.

The bill would let the government block a model's release or use only if it poses a foreseeable, imminent risk of more than $1 billion in damages, or of killing or seriously injuring more than 50 people, according to the report.

Here are some details:

  • The risk must stem from the creation or release of a biological weapon, the model evading its developer’s controls or a cyberattack, Politico reported

  • Anthropic and the Department of Commerce did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment

  • Under the bill, independent evaluators, which would register with the Commerce Department, would be tasked with periodically evaluating the lab and its frontier models, according to the report

  • The labs could pay these evaluators, provided the payment is not tied to the evaluation's outcome, the report said

  • If the evaluators determine there is “imminent enumerated risk” for a company’s frontier models, they must report it to Commerce within 72 hours of completing their assessment, Politico reported

  • While the Commerce Department could request a judge to halt a model after determining risk, the language explicitly prohibits any other US government department, agency, or officer from suspending development, deployment, or internal use, according to the report

  • A federal judge for the District Court for the District of Columbia could order the suspension of a model, the report said

data.title: Juno Industries Completes Qualifying Transaction
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - October 16, 2026) - Juno Industries Ltd. (formerly, Trail Blazer Capital Corp.) (TSXV: TBLZ.P) (the "Company") is pleased to announce that it has completed its acquisition (the "Transaction") of Juno Industries Inc. ("Juno Industries"), which constitutes the "Qualifying Transaction" of the Company pursuant to TSX Venture Exchange (the "Exchange") Policy 2.4 - Capital Pool Companies.

Subject to receipt of final approval of the Exchange, it is anticipated that the common shares of the Company will commence trading on the Exchange under the ticker symbol "JUNO" on or about October 22, 2026 as a Tier 2 Industrial, Technology, and Life Sciences Issuer.

The Transaction

Prior to completing the Transaction, the Company changed its name from "Trail Blazer Capital Corp." to "Juno Industries Ltd." and consolidated its share capital (the "Consolidation") on the basis of 6 (old) common shares (each a "Common Share") for 1 (new) Common Share.

Pursuant to the terms of the Transaction, the Company acquired all of the issued and outstanding shares of Juno Industries through a three-cornered amalgamation involving a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company and Juno Industries. All outstanding securities of Juno Industries were exchanged for post-Consolidation securities of the Company on a 1:1.45 basis (the "Exchange Ratio"). In connection with the Transaction, the Company issued 22,474,996 Common Shares to former shareholders of Juno Industries. Juno Industries will operate as a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company and the Company will continue the business of Juno Industries. Further details regarding the Transaction can be found in the Company's Filing Statement (the "Filing Statement") dated October 13, 2026 filed under the Company's profile on SEDAR+.

In connection with the Transaction, in accordance with the requirements of the Exchange, certain securityholders of the Company have entered into an Exchange Form 5D Escrow Agreement (the "Escrow Agreement") in respect of 9,782,976 Common Shares, 122,500 stock options (each a "Company Option") and 1,786,424 restricted share units (each an "RSU") of the Company. Under the terms of the Escrow Agreement, 10% of such escrowed securities will be released upon issuance of the final bulletin of the Exchange in respect of the Transaction, with subsequent 15% releases occurring 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, and 36 months from such date.

Concurrent Financing

As previously announced, Juno Industries completed a non-brokered subscription receipt financing (the "SR Offering") in two tranches on each of April 24, and April 30, 2026 for gross proceeds of $12,000,000. In connection with the completion of the Transaction, each subscription receipt converted into such number of Juno Industries Shares that resulted in the holder receiving one post-Consolidation Common Share for each subscription receipt held after giving effect to the Exchange Ratio (each a "Subscription Receipt Share") and such Subscription Receipt Shares were immediately exchanged for post-Consolidation Common Shares pursuant to the Transaction. In connection with the conversion of the subscription receipts, the proceeds of the SR Offering were released from escrow.

In connection with the SR Offering, on closing of the Transaction, Juno Industries paid eligible arm's length finders aggregate cash finders fees of $209,100 and the Company issued 262,180 finders warrants to purchase Common Shares ("Finders Warrant"). Each Finders Warrant entitles the holder thereof to purchase one Common Share at a price of $0.80 per Common Share, until October 16, 2028. The arm's length finders that were compensated in connection with the SR Offering were Ventum Financial Corp., Haywood Securities Inc., Acumen Capital Finance Partners Limited, BMO Nesbitt Burns Inc., Canaccord Genuity Corp. ("Canaccord"), Research Capital Corporation, Harbourfront Wealth Management Inc., and Leede Financial Inc.

In connection with the SR Offering, Juno Industries also entered into an advisory agreement with Canaccord whereby Canaccord provided advisory services in connection with the SR Offering. As consideration for Canaccord's services, on closing of the Transaction, the Company paid Canaccord: (i) a cash corporate finance fee of $40,000 (exclusive of applicable taxes); and (ii) issued 150,000 post-Consolidation Common Shares at a deemed price of $0.80 per Common Share, subject to a contractual restriction on resale pursuant to which one-third of the Common Shares issued to Canaccord will be released on each of the 6th, 12th and 18th month anniversaries of the closing date of the Transaction.

The net proceeds from the SR Offering will be used to finance various corporate initiatives, mergers and acquisitions, and general corporate purposes of the Company following the completion of the Transaction. For more information, refer to the Company's Filing Statement, which is available under the Company's profile on SEDAR+.

Board and Management

In connection with the completion of the Transaction, the Company is pleased to announce its Board of Directors as follows: Hon. Harjit S. Sajjan, Hunter Scharfe, Stephen Kukucha, Joseph Guy Claude Yves Rochette, and Alnesh Mohan. In addition, the Company is pleased to announce its executive management as follows: Hunter Scharfe (CEO and President), Hon. Harjit S. Sajjan (Executive Chairman), and Dallas Pretty (CFO and Corporate Secretary).

Option and Restricted Share Unit Grants

In connection with closing of the Transaction, the Company has granted a total of 2,256,000 Company Options and 2,261,875 RSUs to certain directors, officers, employees, and consultants of the Company pursuant to the Company's omnibus equity incentive plan (the "Plan").

Each Company Option is exercisable to acquire one post-Consolidation Common Share at an exercise price of $0.80 per Common Share. The Company Options shall vest over periods ranging from immediately upon grant to two years from date of grant, with 2,131,000 Options expiring three years from the date of grant and 125,000 Options expiring five years from date of grant.

Each RSU expires three (3) years from the grant date, with 2,324,375 RSUs vesting on the date that is one year from the date of grant and 62,500 RSUs vesting on the date that is two years following the date of grant.

All Company Options and RSUs are subject to the terms of the Plan, applicable securities law hold periods and the policies of the Exchange.

Milestone Capital Partners - IFZA

On October 1, 2026, Juno Industries entered into a consulting services agreement (the "Milestone Agreement") with Milestone Capital Partners - IFZA ("Milestone") and the principal of Milestone, Christian Klingebiel of Silicon Oasis, Dubai, U.A.E., pursuant to which Milestone was engaged as a non-exclusive consultant to assist in Juno Industrie's marketing program. The services to be provided under the Milestone Agreement constitute "investor relations activities" as defined in applicable securities laws and the policies of the Exchange.
